children: Patriot Mobile Inc. filed for an initial public offering of its Class A common stock. The Texas-based, values-driven wireless provider plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker “PTRT.” Northland Capital Markets is serving as the sole book-running manager.

Patriot Mobile is a values-driven, nationwide communications company that operates an asset-light mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) model. Instead of owning spectrum or building network infrastructure, the company purchases wholesale capacity through aggregators to access all three major national wireless networks. Patriot Mobile provides postpaid wireless voice, text, and data services, connected devices, device protection, financing, mobile internet and 5G home wireless, along with accessories. The company differentiates through a mission-led brand, 100% U.S.-based customer support, and coverage flexibility that allows customers to move between supported networks if needed.

The company targets consumers, families, businesses, churches, ministries, nonprofits, and other organizations seeking to align purchasing with Christian-conservative values. Revenue is primarily subscription-based, supplemented by device and accessory sales and value-added services. Patriot Mobile emphasizes a diversified, omni-channel acquisition engine (radio/podcasts, television, digital, referrals, affiliates, sponsorships, and events) and a digital-first onboarding experience. Its strategy aims to expand wallet share with offerings like device protection and 5G home wireless, while also pursuing adjacent opportunities (e.g., insurance and other technology services) over time.
: Approximately 28.3 million U.S. adults who identify as “very conservative,” equating to a core SAM of about $15 billion and an expanded opportunity of $40+ billion across adjacent services.
: U.S. wireless data usage reached 132 trillion MB in 2024, growing roughly 35% annually for three consecutive years.
: Asset-light MVNO with access to all three major national wireless networks, targeting values-aligned consumers and organizations.
: AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile; MVNOs such as Consumer Cellular, Google Fi, US Mobile, MobileX, Spectrum Mobile, Xfinity Mobile, and others.
: Rising postpaid churn amid competitive promotions; rapid 5G adoption; increasing demand for bundled and converged connectivity; expanding consumer preference for values-aligned brands.
: Approximately 186,000 active wireless lines as of December 31, 2025; 202,848 as of June 30, 2026
: Headquarters in Grapevine, Texas; nationwide service footprint via multi-network access
: United States (nationwide coverage across all three major national networks)
: Multi-network access via MVNAs; marketing partnerships and sponsorships including NASCAR and SEC football

: Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 86 (as of December 31, 2025); average monthly churn of ~1% in 2025; 2025 ARPU of approximately $543; 100% U.S.-based customer service; launched 5G Home Wireless to consumers in May 2026
, Chief Executive Officer - Co-founder; 25+ years in strategic planning, finance and operations; non-practicing CPA; previously led businesses and finance organizations in New York.
, Chief Operating Officer - 30+ years in corporate finance and investment management with Salomon Brothers, Bankers Trust, Fitch Ratings and C-III Asset Management.
, Chief Financial Officer - Background in private equity, investment banking and portfolio company leadership; experience in capital formation, M&A and operations.
, Chief Marketing Officer - Former co-founder of Rev19; led marketing at a digital agency; prior leadership roles at Sabre Holdings and EDS.
, Chief Technology Officer - 25 years in technology leadership; previously VP of Technology at Avero; expertise in infrastructure, systems integration and scaling platforms.
, General Counsel - Corporate attorney with experience across energy and nonprofit sectors; licensed in Texas and Illinois; focuses on governance and compliance.

: Purchase newly issued LLC Units from Patriot Mobile Holdings LLC; fund redemptions of LLC Units from certain continuing equity holders; repay borrowings under the company’s revolving line of credit; pay offering expenses; and for general corporate purposes including potential acquisitions.
